claims.text: Controlled aging of a eutectic high-entropy alloy can induce stable nanoscale coherent precipitates.
Aging-induced nanoscale coherent precipitates can simultaneously increase yield strength and ductility relative to the as-solidified state.
Precise control of aging parameters can prevent precipitate coarsening.
The initial rapidly solidified alloy has an FCC+B2 eutectic microstructure and lacks aging-induced precipitates.
Aging at 600–700°C for 1–4 hours under an inert atmosphere can produce nanoscale coherent precipitates in the proposed alloy.
Real-time microstructural feedback can be used to restrict precipitation to nanoscale coherent precipitates.
Post-solidification aging under the proposed conditions retains the eutectic microstructure.
The treatment produces nanoscale coherent precipitates both along phase boundaries and within the ductile matrix.
Coherent precipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby increase yield strength.
The precipitates promote dislocation interactions and enhance work hardening.
Enhanced work hardening delays strain localization and necking, thereby increasing ductility.
Optimized aging will increase yield strength by at least approximately 20% relative to the as-solidified alloy.
Optimized aging will increase total elongation and work hardening relative to the as-solidified alloy.
Significant deviations in aging temperature, duration, or monitoring can cause precipitate coarsening or incoherent-phase formation.
Precipitate coarsening or incoherent-phase formation can degrade ductility.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as an as-solidified, rapidly quenched eutectic HEA, whereas the experimental control is called as-cast. As-cast and rapidly quenched states may have different microstructures and are not established as equivalent.
